title: Update by the full key
summary: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values.
introduction: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values. Your task: Read the same key after the update.
learningObjectives: Read the same key after the update.
Explain the example for update by the full key

blocks.text: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values. Cassandra writes can create missing non-key values at that address.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code: UPDATE reading_by_reader SET pages=25 WHERE reader_id='mia' AND day='2026-11-16';
blocks.title: Update by the full key

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.text: The page count at that exact reader-and-day address becomes 25.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not assume UPDATE proves the old row existed. If that matters, learn conditional writes and their cost.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Read the same key after the update.
